newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST - Italy discount rate to ease end-October.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Italy discount rate to ease end-October.

text.p: The Bank of Italy is likely to cut official interest rates by the end of October, a Reuter survey of 12 economists showed on Friday, with half of those polled seeing an easing of between 50 and 75 basis points.
All of those asked expected the central bank to ease monetary policy, with 75 percent expecting a cut by the end of October and the remaining 25 percent seeing a reduction by the end of the year.
The central bank last decided to lower its discount rate to 8.25 percent from 9.00 and its fixed term advances or Lombard rate to 9.75 percent from 10.50 on July 23.
Speculation the Bank of Italy would lower rates soon has circulated in financial markets after the government announced a larger than expected budget deficit cutting package for 1997.
But the central bank said earlier on Friday its monetary policy remained aimed at pushing average inflation below 3.0 percent in 1997. Inflation is currently at 3.4 percent on a year on year basis.

Analysts said factors affecting the forecasts would be the length of time it takes parliament to approve the 1997 budget, which must be passed by the year end, and the inflationary impact of renewed labour contracts in the engineering sector.
However, a quarter of those polled expected the central bank to cut by at least 50 basis points, and another 25 percent expected a 75 basis point easing.
Some 16 percent saw a reduction of 0.75 point or more, while four of those asked expected an overall easing of 100 to 125 basis points made in two steps by the year end.
Following are the results of the survey:
1. Will the Bank of Italy cut the discount rate?
Yes 100.0 pct (12 out of 12)
2. When will this rate cut take place?
By end October 75.0 pct (9/12)
By end of year 25.0 pct (3/12)
3. By how much will the central bank cut the discount rate?
50 basis points 25.0 pct (3/12)
100-125 in 2 tranches 33.3 pct (4/12)
Note - The table shows only those cuts expected by the end of the year. Four analysts expected the Bank of Italy would cut the discount rate further in 1997 by 50 to 125 basis points.
Participants were Banca di Roma, Banco di Sardegna, Bank of America, Caboto, Chase Manhattan Bank, Banca Commerciale Italiana, Credito Italiano, Deutsche Bank, DRI, IRS, NatWest and San Paolo.
